S71.01.note: Drawer swipe is set in src/features/shell/drawerGestures.ts; the app opens the drawer on phones by a left-edge swipe.
steps: Open AGI Mobile and sign in. Swipe right from the left edge of the screen.
Look: a drawer slides in from the left over the screen.
Tap "Library" in the drawer.
Look: the Library screen opens as a new page on top of the drawer's screen.
Swipe from the left edge of the Library screen (or tap the back control at the top left).
Look: you return to the previous screen, the way a stack route with a back gesture should.
S71.01.where: Any main screen > swipe right from the left edge to open the drawer, then tap "New chat" or "Library"

S71.02.note: The growth cap is maxHeight 160 on the message input in ChatInput.tsx.
steps: Open a chat, or tap "New chat" in the drawer.
Tap the message box and type one short line. Look: a single-line pill.
Keep typing until the text wraps onto a second line. Look: the box grows taller, up to a limit, and a small expand button appears at its top-right.
Tap "Expand message". Look: a full-screen editor titled by the field "Expanded message input" opens.
Type a little more, then tap "Send message" (the send button). Look: the message is sent and the editor closes.
S71.02.where: Chat screen > message box (placeholder "Type or hold to talk") > "Expand message" button at its top-right corner once the text wraps

S71.03.note: On a Mac Simulator the software keyboard can be shown with I/O > Keyboard > Toggle Software Keyboard if no keyboard appears.
steps: Open any chat.
Tap "Message input" at the bottom of the screen. The software keyboard rises.
Look: the message box and send controls sit above the keyboard, not under it.
Look: the last message in the chat stays visible above the composer.
Dismiss the keyboard and check that the layout returns to its normal place.

S71.04.note: Expected says share and rate are tap targets on the message, but the tap row in the code has only copy, read aloud, regenerate and a more-actions button; share and rate appear only in the long-press menu (rate) or on images and files.
steps: Open a chat that has an assistant reply.
Look under the reply for a small row of icon buttons.
Tap the copy button. Look: it shows a check mark, and the text is on the clipboard.
Tap "Read aloud". Look: the reply is spoken, and the button changes to "Stop reading aloud".
Tap "Regenerate response". Look: a new answer to the same question appears.
Compare with Expected: the row has copy, read aloud and regenerate; share and rate are not on this row. Rate is in the long-press menu as "Good Response" and "Bad Response".
S71.04.where: Chat screen > below an assistant reply: the row of buttons "Copy", "Read aloud", "Regenerate response" and "More message actions"

S71.05.note: The long-press menu list is in MessageBubble.tsx around lines 1643 to 1725; the screen-reader versions use lower-case labels such as "Edit message". I did not check whether Delete asks for confirmation.
steps: Open a chat with one of your messages and one assistant reply.
Press and hold your message for about half a second. Look: a menu of actions opens.
Tap "Edit Message", change a word and submit the edit. Look: the edited message and a new answer appear.
Press and hold the assistant reply, tap "Copy Message". Look: the text is copied.
Press and hold the reply again, tap "Export Message". Look: the export sheet opens.
Compare with Expected: each menu item should run what its name says.
S71.05.where: Chat screen > long-press (press and hold) a message bubble > menu with "Edit Message", "Retry", "Copy Message", "Export Message", "Delete Message", "Good Response", "Bad Response"

S71.06.needs: a real iPhone with a camera (the Mac Simulator has no camera)
S71.06.note: The camera screen is blocked when camera access is denied (app/(app)/camera.tsx uses the canUseCamera capability check).
steps: Open a chat and tap "Add to chat".
Tap "Camera" in the sheet. Allow camera access if the phone asks.
Tap "Take photo" on the camera screen.
Look: the camera screen closes and the photo appears as an attachment above the message box.
Send a message and check that the photo goes with it.
S71.06.where: Chat screen > "Add to chat" (the + beside the message box) > "Camera" > "Take photo"

S71.07.needs: a photo library with at least two photos
S71.07.note: Multiple selection is on, with a limit that depends on plan and mode (app/(app)/chat/[id].tsx around line 1580).
steps: Open a chat and tap "Add to chat".
Tap "Photos". Allow access to the photo library if asked.
Select two or more photos in the system picker and confirm.
Look: each selected photo appears as an attachment above the message box, in the order picked.
Send the message and check the photos are attached.

S71.08.needs: a file to upload, for example a PDF in Files
S71.08.note: The picker is opened with multiple selection on (app/(app)/chat/[id].tsx around line 1606).
steps: Open a chat and tap "Add to chat".
Tap "File". The system document picker opens.
Choose one or more files (for example a PDF) and confirm.
Look: each file appears as an attachment chip above the message box.
Send the message and check the file is attached.

S71.09.needs: a phone with the app installed; a web page, an image or a PDF to share
S71.09.note: The share sheet name of the app was not confirmed in the code; the share extension is set up in app.config.js.
steps: On a phone with the app installed, open Safari and go to any web page.
Tap Share, then choose the AGI app from the share sheet.
Look: the share preview screen opens with the shared content shown.
For a link, check for "Summarize this page" and "Ask about this page".
Tap "Send to Chat" (or "Add to chat" if files are staged). Look: a chat starts or the files are attached.
S71.09.where: Another app (for example Safari) > Share > the AGI app in the share sheet > the preview screen with "Send to Chat" or "Add to chat"

S71.10.needs: a microphone, and a phone that supports live voice
S71.10.note: Full-duplex behaviour (talking over the reply) was not confirmed in the code; if voice is unavailable the app shows a reason from liveVoiceModeUnavailableReason.
steps: Open a chat and tap "Start voice mode". Allow microphone access if asked.
Look: the voice bar replaces the composer.
Say a question and pause. Look: the assistant answers out loud.
Ask a follow-up in the same voice session and check it continues without tapping.
Tap "Exit voice mode" to stop. Look: the normal composer returns.
S71.10.where: Chat screen > "Start voice mode" (round button at the right of the composer)

S71.12.needs: a real iPhone; an AGI Cloud account; a running agent task for the push test
S71.12.note: Whether push registration works on the Mac Simulator was not checked in the code; the token storage and server sends are not visible in the UI.
steps: Tap Settings, then find the "Device" section and tap "Notifications".
Read the status card at the top: "Turn on notifications", "Your device is delivering notifications" or "Your device is blocking notifications".
If the card says "Turn on notifications", tap it or the allow control and accept the iOS prompt.
Look: the card changes to "Your device is delivering notifications" and the list below shows which alerts AGI sends.
The server-side token storage and the pushes themselves cannot be seen on the phone; check that alerts arrive when an agent task finishes.

S71.13.needs: an AGI Cloud account; a notification that links to a task, approval, schedule or chat
S71.13.note: The deep link routes are in app/(app)/open/[target]/[id].tsx; the banner tap itself needs a real device.
steps: Trigger a notification, for example by finishing an agent task or a schedule.
Tap the banner on the phone. Or tap the bell button ("Open notifications, N unread") at the top of the drawer header.
Tap the row in the Notifications list.
Look: the screen opens that the notification is about (task, approval, schedule or chat).
Compare with Expected: the right screen opens, not the home screen.
S71.13.where: Notification banner on the phone, or the bell button ("Open notifications") > tap a row in the Notifications list

S71.14.needs: a Cloud task that is waiting for an answer
S71.14.note: I did not check whether a notification can carry a reply action; only the in-app answer form was found.
steps: Open the drawer (swipe right from the left edge) and tap "AGI Work".
Tap a Cloud task that shows a question from the agent.
Fill in the answer form that appears under the task details.
Tap "Send answer".
Look: the question disappears and the task status moves on from waiting for input.
S71.14.where: AGI Work > tap a task that is waiting for an answer > fill the question form > "Send answer"

S71.15.needs: a Cloud task that is waiting for an approval
S71.15.note: The desktop-side remote approval (Remote control) is hidden in v1 because FEATURES.companion is false in apps/mobile/lib/v1FeatureFlags.ts; only the Cloud task approval is reachable.
steps: Open the drawer and tap "AGI Work".
Tap a Cloud task that shows a pending action needing approval.
Read the tool call listed in the task.
Tap "Approve" (or "Deny").
Look: the pending approval disappears and the task resumes (or stops, after deny).
S71.15.where: AGI Work > tap a task that is waiting for approval > "Approve" or "Deny"

S71.16.needs: a paid account and a paired computer (the Remote feature is off in v1)
S71.16.note: The remote code session screens are gated by FEATURES.companion = false (apps/mobile/lib/v1FeatureFlags.ts line 16) and show a "Remote" unavailable message (app/(app)/companion/code/[threadId].tsx). The Remote control settings row is also hidden. I searched the app folder for the remote code session screens and Remote control entry points.

S71.17.note: The start flow is in src/features/tasks/startWork.ts; the exact position of "New task" on screen was not checked.
steps: Open the drawer and tap "AGI Work".
Tap "New task".
Type what the task should do and start it.
Look: the new task appears at the top of the AGI Work task list with a status.
Tap it to open the task and check its activity.

S71.19.needs: a signed-in account with a chat that has messages
S71.19.note: The Code line points at a line in MessageBubble.tsx that is now an animation setting; the draft store is src/features/chat/draftStore.ts and in-flight recovery is src/features/chat/inFlightTurnRecovery.ts.
steps: Open a chat, type a draft in the message box, but do not send it.
Force-quit AGI Mobile (on the Simulator: Cmd+Shift+H twice, then swipe the app card up).
Open the app again from the home screen.
Look: the same chat opens with the draft still in the message box and the earlier messages still shown.
If a reply was in progress, check that it resumes or shows as finished, as Expected says.
S71.19.where: Effect seen after the app is force-quit and reopened, on the chat screen

S71.25.note: The layout switches at 768 px (TABLET_MIN_WIDTH) and 1024 px (REGULAR_MIN_WIDTH) in src/shared/hooks/useTabletLayout.ts.
steps: Open the app on an iPad (the app is set to support tablets in app.config.js).
Look: the drawer stays on the left side as a fixed panel, not a slide-out.
Look: the chat area is wider and the message grid is laid out in more columns.
Turn the iPad or change split view width and check the layout adapts.
Compare with Expected: persistent drawer and wider layout on tablets.
S71.25.where: Effect seen on an iPad or iPad Simulator; the drawer stays visible on the left

S71.27.needs: a phone or Simulator that can rotate
S71.27.note: Phones are locked to portrait (app/_layout.tsx calls lockPhonePortrait; app.config.js sets orientation portrait). Landscape is only used while a video player or presentation viewer is open. The iPad behaviour was not checked.
steps: Open a chat on a phone.
Turn the phone sideways (on the Simulator, use Cmd+Left or Cmd+Right).
Look: the chat stays in portrait layout.
Compare with Expected: Expected says landscape re-lays out the chat usefully, but the code locks phones to portrait.
S71.27.where: Effect seen when a phone is turned sideways with a chat open; the screen should stay upright

S71.28.needs: a downloaded model (for the model delete step, see S71.30); a test account for the delete-all step
S71.28.note: Clear cache asks first with the title "Clear cache?" (app/(app)/settings/storage.tsx around line 289).
steps: Tap Settings, go to the "Device" section, tap "Storage".
Look at "Downloaded models (estimated)", "Cache" and "Free space" figures.
Tap "Clear cache" and confirm. Look: the cache figure drops and conversations and models stay.
If a downloaded model is listed, tap "Delete <model name>" and confirm. Look: the model is removed from the list.
Tap "Delete all local data" only on a test account, since it wipes conversations, memory and models from this device.

S71.30.needs: Wi-Fi for the download; enough free storage; a phone (Simulator may not run on-device models)
S71.30.note: I did not find the exact control that switches a chat from Cloud to Local mode; the picker's On device group is the route found. Check the mode before relying on the steps.
steps: Open a new chat. Tap the model button beside the + (it reads "Model:" followed by the model name).
In the model picker, find the "On device" group and tap a model to download it.
Tap "Download" in the confirmation. Look: the download starts and the storage size is shown.
When the download finishes, pick that model, type a message and send it.
Look: a reply comes from the model on the device. Turn Wi-Fi and cellular off on the phone to check it needs no cloud.
S71.30.where: Chat screen > "Model:" button beside the + in the composer (opens the model picker) > "On device" group > download a model

S71.31.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account; an App Store or Google Play test account for a real restore
S71.31.note: Purchases are switched off: FEATURES.billing is false in apps/mobile/lib/v1FeatureFlags.ts, and src/features/billing/service.ts throws 'cloud billing not available in v1'. Only the restore screen is reachable.
steps: Tap Settings, go to the "Account" section, tap "Subscription".
Look: if the store is not live you will see "Purchases are not available right now".
Tap "Restore purchases". Look: a message appears such as "No purchases to restore" or "Restore purchases needs the store".
Compare with Expected: buying a plan or credits is not switched on in v1, so the buy path cannot be tested yet.

S71.32.needs: a device with Face ID or Touch ID set up (not checked on the Simulator)
S71.32.note: The privacy cover on app switch was not found: searched apps/mobile for privacy cover, app switch and AppState usage and found nothing.
steps: Tap Settings, go to the "Device" section, tap "Safety & Security".
Under "Device boundary", turn on the "App Lock" switch and follow the device prompt.
Close the app and open it again. Look: an app lock screen asks you to unlock before the chat shows.
Tap "Permissions" and look at the list of phone permissions (camera, microphone, photos, notifications).
Compare with Expected: App Lock and OS permission management are present; no privacy cover on app switch was found in the code.
S71.32.where: Settings > Device > Safety & Security > "App Lock" and "Permissions"
